702376.t: From βαθύς (bathús, “deep”) + -ος (-os), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʷeh₂dʰ- (“to sink, submerge”) (though Beekes rejects the link to the Indo-European root).

702381.t: Zero-grade of the root of βένθος (bénthos), of uncertain origin. Alternatively from earlier *βαφύς (*baphús), related to Sanskrit गभीर (gabhīrá, “deep”).

702375.t: From the root of βαίνω (baínō, “to go”).

702305.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂égʰos, from the root *h₂egʰ- (“to be upset, in distress, afraid”). Compare Sanskrit अ॒घ (aghá, “evil”), Proto-Germanic *agaz (“fear”) (Gothic 𐌰𐌲𐌹𐍃 (agis), dialectal English ey).

702367.t: βάδην (bádēn), from βαίνω (baínō), with the suffix -ίζω (-ízō).

702313.t: Zero grade of μέχρι (mékhrĭ), from Proto-Indo-European *méǵʰ(s)ri. The genitive is from the PIE ablative of comparison/extent.

702309.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + χρεία (khreía, “need; use”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

702316.t: According to Beekes, from Pre-Greek and related to ἄχωρ (ákhōr, “scurf”) (particularly, identical to the form ἄχορα (ákhora)) and to ἄχνη (ákhnē, “foam, froth”).
